newsitem.title: THAILAND: Goh seeks to boost telecom links with Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Goh seeks to boost telecom links with Thailand.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on Monday urged Thailand to join a strategic high-speed telecommunications network linking his country with the United States.
A Thai government spokesman said Goh also told his Thai counterpart Chavalit Yongchaiyudh that Singapore recognised Thailand's crucial role as the future hub of trade and industries in Indochina.
"The Singapore prime minister asked if Thailand would be interested in being part of the strategic network," the spokesman, Varathep Ratanakorn, told reporters.
"This would be a comprehensive telecommunications cooperation in economic, educational and information technology fields."
Last month, Singapore launched a high-speed Internet link to the United States, the first country in Asia after Japan to do so.
Ratanakorn said a contingent of more than 70 Singapore businessmen who accompanied Goh on a three-day visit showed Singapore was confident in Thailand's economy despite its current setbacks.
The weak Thai economy, rocked by problems in its battered financial and property sectors, is this year projected to grow at its slowest pace in a decade.
Ratanakorn said Goh praised Thailand's eastern and southern seaboard projects as a vital future infrastructure base for the Indochinese region that also covers Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and Burma.
Goh arrived in Bangkok on Monday. He was due to have an audience with King Bhumibol Adulyadej later in the day and tour industrial zones in south eastern Thailand on Tuesday.
"The Thai economy faces some problems today. But we are confident that when our project is completed in eight years, Thailand's economy will grow," said visiting Singapore businessman Dominic Ng.

Ng is managing director of JTC International Pte Ltd. His company signed a $720 million joint venture with Eastern Sugar Co Ltd of Thailand on Monday to develop an industrial estate in the eastern Rayong province.
Ratanakorn said Goh discussed with Chavalit and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan the possibility of relaxing bilateral civil aviation restrictions.
But he said the two leaders did not touch on plans by the Bank of Thailand to seek Singapore advice on revamping its foreign exchange regime for the Thai baht.
Thailand took steps to cut off baht supply for currency speculators in its bid to defend the currency during a severe speculative attack in May.
